name: CeraVe

lead:
CeraVe is a dermatology-oriented skincare brand, founded in 2005 and owned by L'Oreal, whose cleansers and moisturizers are marketed on ceramide content. Ceramides are lipids found in the skin barrier.
Its appeal for looks is a simple, inexpensive routine for dry, acne-prone or sensitive skin, so skin looks and feels more even and comfortable. It was a staple of 2020 skincare-influencer routines.

paras: Users add a cleanser and moisturizer to a basic routine, commonly with sunscreen and with actives such as tretinoin. Some forum members use it as the gentle base around acne treatment.
Moisturizers can occasionally trigger allergic contact dermatitis. A looksmax.org thread questions ceramide products on hormonal grounds, but that is a community claim.

angle.text: A moisturizing routine keeps skin comfortable and hydrated, which helps skin look smoother and supports actives like tretinoin.

lead: CeraVe is a drugstore skincare brand of cleansers, moisturizers, sunscreens and acne products, advertised on its ceramide content. Ceramides are lipids found in the outer layer of skin, and a routine built around a gentle cleanser and a moisturizer is how people use the brand to keep skin hydrated and calm, which supports a smoother, more even-looking complexion [1].

The company was founded in 2005 under Bausch Health (then Valeant) and was bought by L'Oreal in 2017, together with AcneFree and Ambi, for 1.3 billion dollars [1]. Its products are mainly used for acne, eczema and dry skin; a New York Times review cited by Wikipedia found the moisturizing cream contains ceramides, glycerin and petrolatum [1]. Global sales rose 89 percent in 2020 after skincare influencer Hyram Yarbro promoted it, and the brand ran a 2024 Super Bowl ad with actor Michael Cera [1].

Published research includes a randomized forearm study of four over-the-counter moisturizers including CeraVe Moisturizing Cream, company-linked consumer and itch studies of CeraVe formulations, a basic-regimen comparison that used CeraVe cleanser, and a patch-test analysis of moisturizer ingredients [2][3][1][4][5][6]. In looksmaxxing forums it appears as a budget base routine, including beside tretinoin.

paras: The brand sells facial and body cleansers, moisturizing creams and lotions, sunscreens, and acne and itch-relief products [1]. Marketing emphasizes ceramides, and Wikipedia notes that products are mainly used for acne, eczema and dry skin [1]. Specific formulations differ by product: for example, one body cleanser and cream studied in people with psoriasis combined ceramides with salicylic acid and urea, and an itch-relief line added 1 percent pramoxine [1][5].

sections.h: How it is used for appearance
paras: People use a cleanser and moisturizer as the simple base of a routine, usually alongside sunscreen and sometimes with acne actives such as tretinoin; the moisturizer's job in these routines is to keep skin hydrated and less irritated so the skin surface looks smoother. A basic-regimen comparison after laser resurfacing used CeraVe cleanser with Aquaphor, Vanicream and sunscreen as the comparison routine, showing the brand is also used as a plain base in dermatology settings [4]. T Nation forum posters have also mentioned CeraVe cleansers while managing acne, including a salicylic-acid cleanser used on the face, back and shoulders [7][8].

CeraVe was founded in 2005 and was owned by Bausch Health, then known as Valeant [1]. In 2017 Valeant sold it to L'Oreal for 1.3 billion dollars, along with AcneFree and Ambi, and it sits within L'Oreal's Dermatological Beauty division [1].

Between March and October 2020, skincare influencer Hyram Yarbro promoted the brand heavily; his videos reportedly generated 3.2 million dollars in media impact value, and the brand reported global sales up 89 percent that year [1]. In February 2024 it aired a Super Bowl LVIII commercial with Michael Cera, playing on the similarity between the two names [1].

In a randomized, observer-blind forearm study, patients with atopic dermatitis applied one of four moisturizers (Cetaphil Cream, Aveeno Eczema Therapy, CeraVe Moisturizing Cream or Vaseline) to one forearm for four weeks, with the other forearm untreated. Twenty patients completed it; skin capacitance (hydration) improved significantly on the moisturized arm, while the change in transepidermal water loss was not significant, and the authors report that recruitment fell short of target [2].

Two double-blind, split-body studies in 66 people with atopic history tested CeraVe Itch Relief lotion and cream, which contain ceramides and 1 percent pramoxine, comparing onset and duration of itch relief, including against 1 percent hydrocortisone cream [3]. A consumer usage study of CeraVe body cleanser and cream with ceramides, salicylic acid and urea involved 33 adults with mild-to-moderate psoriasis, applying the cream twice daily for two weeks and reporting by questionnaire [5]. A split-face trial of a procedural enhancement system versus a basic regimen (Aquaphor, CeraVe cleanser, Vanicream, sunscreen) after thulium laser resurfacing found the enhancement system rated better at day 4; CeraVe was part of the comparison regimen [4]. A Lemmy skincare thread links a split-face, double-blind randomized trial of a ceramide and niacinamide cream (CeraVe PM) added to topical acne treatment, and notes that the study was described as not industry sponsored [9]. A 2025 review of eczema ointments lists CeraVe Moisturizing Cream among common over-the-counter eczema skin products [6].

A 2020 analysis of three common moisturizer brands (Aveeno, Cetaphil and CeraVe) counted 12, 14 and 9 potential allergens respectively; most were infrequent allergens not included in standard patch-test series, and the authors suggest targeted testing when contact dermatitis is suspected [10].

One looksmax.org member posted a purchase of CeraVe blemish control and moisturizing lotion with tretinoin and asked for thoughts; a reply said tretinoin was the most useful item in the set. Another thread asks for a routine without CeraVe-type products, with the poster saying such cosmetics harm the skin barrier and contain estrogen-like ingredients, and mentioning tallow soap; a reply suggested olive oil at night [11]. These are member claims.

lore.intro: CeraVe appears on looksmax.org as a basic moisturizer and acne-routine base, and one thread debates whether such products affect skin dependence or hormones [11].
